title: Catch-all route at the root level doesn't work any more in .NET 8
body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

I have an application with very few pages, where one is mainly active and catches all the remaining URLs as a part of its logic. In .NET 7, It was enough to annotate that page with `@page "/{*pageRoute}"` and declare the corresponding parameter `[Parameter] public string? PageRoute { get; set; }`. But it stopped working when I upgraded to .NET 8 (Blazor United) and started showing a white screen and an exception in the browser's console.

### Expected Behavior

It should catch the rest of the URLs that didn't match with other routes .

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a net .NET 8 Blazor United app with interactive web assembly with pre-rendering turned OFF.
2. Delete pages but the Index.
3. Annotate the Index page with `@page "/{*pageRoute}"` and declare a parameter for it `[Parameter] public string? PageRoute { get; set; }`
4. Run the app; you should see a white screen with an error in the console.

### Exceptions (if any)

```
blazor.web.js:1  Error: One or more errors occurred. ('<' is an invalid start of a value. LineNumber: 0 | BytePositionInLine: 0.)
    at Jn (marshal-to-js.ts:349:18)
    at Ul (marshal-to-js.ts:306:28)
    at 00b1e8b6:0x1faca
    at 00b1e8b6:0x1bf8b
    at 00b1e8b6:0xf172
    at 00b1e8b6:0x1e7e4
    at 00b1e8b6:0x1efda
    at 00b1e8b6:0xcfec
    at 00b1e8b6:0x440ad
    at e.<computed> (cwraps.ts:338:24)
callEntryPoint @ blazor.web.js:1
```

### .NET Version

8.0.100

### Anything else?

It works if the catch-all wildcard is not placed at the root level but after a URI segment.
We need a way to allow routes without explicitly listing them in razor pages.
author: gdar91

comments.body:
@gdar91 thanks for contacting us.

In .NET 8.0 routing is integrated with ASP.NET Core routing, what's happening is that your route is "too general" and is intercepting requests for files. You need to add `:nonfile` to the route to avoid capturing paths with an extension.

> @gdar91 thanks for contacting us.
> 
> In .NET 8.0 routing is integrated with ASP.NET Core routing, what's happening is that your route is "too general" and is intercepting requests for files. You need to add `:nonfile` to the route to avoid capturing paths with an extension.

Thank you, it worked with `:nonfile`. I changed the attribute to this: `@page "/{*pageRoute:nonfile}"`.

satisfaction_conditions: A solution that allows catch-all routes at the root level to work in .NET 8
An explanation of why the previously working approach no longer functions in .NET 8
A specific syntax modification that prevents the route from capturing unwanted paths
A way to maintain the catch-all functionality for legitimate routes while avoiding conflicts

title: Blazor WebAssembly not caching in browser
body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

Blazor WebAssembly is caching libraries to browser's Cache Storage only on localhost access.

When i was starting to develop WASM project, i've inspected browser cache to make sure that dotnet and other libraries are cached and next startups are faster (sha checks, returned statuses 204, cache is used). This works well. But after publishing the project to IIS hosting and accessing the page over the internet, libraries are never stored in browser cache. So effectively, libraries are always downloaded. Running browser on the same machine where the IIS is located works and libraries are cached (same as running browser directly from VS in development). I've tried this on default projects in .net6 and .net7 and the behaviour is the same.

I must be missing something basic here...

### Expected Behavior

Libraries are cached to browser regardless if the page is accessed localy or remotely over the internet.

### Steps To Reproduce

In VS:

- create new "Blazor WebAssembly App"
- check off "Configure for HTTPS"
- publish (i'm using just the directory publish with manual copy of files to created web page on iis)

### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

7.0.302

### Anything else?

_No response_
author: ns6000

comments.body:
@ns6000 thanks for contacting us.

Caching depends on the caching APIs that are only available in secure context. We don't do caching over HTTP because the APIs are not available.

Thank you, understood. It will be accessible over HTTPS only in the real world production deployment so it's not a problem.

Just a humble suggestion, I think this could be mentioned somewhere in the docs (if it's not already and I missed it).

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of why Blazor WebAssembly caching works differently between local and remote environments
Confirmation that HTTPS deployment will enable proper caching functionality
Information about browser caching requirements for Blazor WebAssembly

title: ElementReference causes "Invalid JSON" exception when returned to JavaScript
author: HughPH

comments.body:
Thanks for contacting us, @HughPH.
`ElementReference` is a reference to a DOM element that Blazor has rendered. It cannot be used to refer an element rendered by JavaScript as Blazor has no knowledge of it. You can pass the element id from JavaScript to Blazor and then use it as string internally.

@mkArtakMSFT Thanks for the reply, that makes sense. I had expected that Blazor would 'foster'  (temporarily adopt) unknown elements and create a new _internalId for them, keeping them immutable but referable, then 'translate' them back to their JavaScript object references when being passed back across the divide.

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of ElementReference's limitations with JavaScript-created DOM elements
A clarification of the proper approach for referencing JavaScript-created elements in Blazor
An understanding of the boundary between Blazor and JavaScript interoperability

title: httpContext.Response.OnStarting lambdas executing in reverse order
author: mtamrakar

comments.body: @anurse I'm not sure `hosting` is the right area for this. Can you please adjust as necessary? Thanks!

This is intentional to mirror the middleware pipeline ordering. E.g. The last thing to register is the inner most component in the pipeline and so it gets to look at the response first.

Should update the doc comments to reflect this.

That said, what specific guidance did you get for using OnStarting? It's one of the harder APIs to use correctly, especially with complex interactions like this. You might do better to abstract the cookie handling to centralized logic and restrict to a single OnStarting event to apply the aggregate result.
Your second example is fine if you check HttpContext.Response.HasStarted first. No cookies can be modified after HasStarted, even with OnStarting.
Ideally, when would we ever do the OnStarting registration then?
OnStarting is useful for last second sanity checks, not much else.

Thank you. I'm closing the issue as OnStarting is doing what it supposed to and I do see that a comment update is in progress to clarify it's execution order.

I think we will just go with direct updates and handle out of sequence header updates more carefully.

satisfaction_conditions: Confirmation of the expected behavior of HttpContext.Response.OnStarting
Guidance on best practices for cookie management in ASP.NET Core
Clarification on appropriate use cases for OnStarting
Understanding of how to handle response headers that might be modified from different parts of the code
